8.t: Working with data: weighing the evidence
q: Identify the sources whose D/H could match ocean water, within their uncertainty.
Carbonaceous meteorites, Hartley 2 and 46P/Wirtanen.
Calculate how many times higher the ratio of comet 67P is than that of the oceans.
After Hartley 2, a headline said "Comets brought Earth’s water". Evaluate this claim using all the data.

Only 2 of about 10 comets match, and both have large uncertainties. Most comets are far too high. Meteorites match consistently over about 30 samples, so asteroids are the better-supported main source; comets may have added a little.
Suggest why the D/H of one comet is much less certain than that of ocean water.
Comets are measured remotely from small amounts of gas, often in one visit; ocean water can be sampled directly and measured many times.
Explain why D/H is a useful clue to where Earth’s water came from.
The ratio is set by the temperature where the water formed (colder, farther from the Sun gives more D), and it changes little afterwards, so it acts like a fingerprint.

18.t: Working with data: which planet could hold water?
q: Identify the planets that lie inside their star’s habitable zone.
P, Q and S.
P is in the habitable zone but is frozen. Suggest why.
P has little mass, so weak gravity: it cannot hold a thick atmosphere, so there is little greenhouse warming and no liquid water.
R has the same mass as Earth. Explain its surface temperature of 460 °C.
It is too close to its star, so it receives much more energy; any water evaporated and a runaway greenhouse effect followed, as on Venus.
S always keeps one face towards its star. Discuss whether S or Q is the better target in the search for life.

Q: Sun-like star, temperature allows liquid water, mass can hold an atmosphere. S: in the zone, but one side is very hot and the other frozen, and red dwarfs give off flares that strip atmospheres. Liquid water might exist near the boundary. Q is the better target, but S cannot be ruled out.
State two features, not in the table, that would make liquid water more likely.
Any two: a magnetic field; water vapour detected in the atmosphere; volcanoes or plate movements recycling gases; a stable orbit and tilt.
